messages:
mike: Canary promotion stuck — smoke + e2e failing intermittently right after deploybot prefetch. Seeing a bunch of 504s hitting the shared cache during integration stage :grimacing:

deploy-bot: Promotion to canary queued -> FAILED checks. auto-retry in 15m. Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/3424681357 :robot_face:

karen: Ugh. Is this the same cache-ttl regression we saw last week? :eyes:

sam: Not identical but related. Reproduced locally with `make e2e --stage=ingest` — batch ingest stage times out when multiple workers hit kv-cache regenerate path.

sam: Failed snippet:
```
AssertionError: expected 200 != 504
File tests/e2e/test_ingest.py:47
  requests.get("/v1/ingest?batch=5") -> 504 Gateway Timeout
  502/503/504 spike when cache prefetch throttles
```

jen: QA: flakiness rate ~ 7% on CI today, but 0% on single-run. Looks like concurrency interacts with TTL/regen. I can run a focused sharded job on staging to stress it if you want.

chris: Might be the prefetch/backoff bump in the new image. We changed kv-cache TTL refresh to async+prefetch last deploy. If prefetch fails we fall back but that fallback path is saturating upstream.

mike: Options: A) hold canary until patch, B) rollpin to last-good image tag, or C) pin deploybot to reduce concurrency during promo window. Thoughts?

karen: If patch likely fast, hold. If not, rollpin to `r2026-03-18-201` (last green). We need to avoid breaking customer-facing canaries.

sam: Patch could be small (add jitter + exponential backoff around regen). I can open PR but it needs QA cycles. ETA ~2-4 hours.

jen: For release window we should probably rollpin to be safe. We can run the patch as a separate hotfix canary after hours.

chris: Agree rollpin. Also recommend adding a temporary deploybot throttle flag: `--max-parallel-promotes=4` as a follow-up to reduce blast radius next time.

mike: Decision: HOLD promotion and DO NOT promote further canaries for next 15m while we decide, then ROLLPIN if we don't have a verified patch in 2 hours. I'm creating a short rollback playbook and notifying Release Notes owners.

mike: Rollback doc (draft): <https://go/release/rollback/3424681357> — steps: 1) pin service image to `r2026-03-18-201`, 2) restart canary router pods, 3) monitor token-level error rates for 20m, 4) notify #incidents if >1% error.

deploy-bot: Acknowledged. Holding promotions for canary group "canary-ingest". Next auto-retry suppressed.

sam: I'll start the jitter/backoff PR and link here. Running targeted staging sharded job now — will post results in ~30m.

jen: Notifying release notes and product that the canary is on hold. Adding a note to the release checklist: "blocked by cache-regen flake".

karen: Thanks. If we end up rolling back, please include the exact image digest in the rollout message so downstream teams can pin quickly.

mike: Will do. Updating release status: HOLD -> possible rollback in 2h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
